title: Baron’s fourth assertion: some regenerate sins rightly called venial under the gracious covenant
source_text: XXXVI. Quarta vero ejus assertio haec est, Quaedam regenitorum peccata recte dicuntur venialia; quia juxta gratiosum Dei foedus, & paternam benignitatem, non excludunt illos a spe regni coelestis, aut ab eo favoris gradu quo prius a Deo diligebantur. Cujusmodi pec-cata dicit esse rebelles & involuntarios concupiscentiae motus; item defectus & naevos, qui bonis renatorum operibus adhaerescunt. Denique ea quae ex materiae parvitate venialia vocantur; quia videlicet in re levi, aut minoris momenti committuntur. De quibus peccatis Scripturam loqui censet Jac. 3. In multis offendimus omnes, & 1 Joh. 1. Si dixerimus nos peccatum non habere fallimus nos ipsos, & veritas in nobis non est, & Ecclesiastae 7. Non est homo justus in terra, qui faciat bonum & non peccet.
pass_a_gloss: But his fourth assertion is this: Certain sins of the regenerate are rightly called venial; because according to God’s gracious covenant and paternal kindness they do not exclude them from the hope of the heavenly kingdom, or from that degree of favor by which they were formerly loved by God. Of which sort he says are rebellious and involuntary motions of concupiscence; likewise defects and blemishes that cling to the good works of the regenerate. Finally those which from smallness of matter are called venial; because namely they are committed in a light matter, or of lesser moment. Concerning which sins he judges Scripture to speak in James 3, In many things we all offend, and 1 John 1, If we say that we have no sin we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us, and Ecclesiastes 7, There is not a just man upon earth who does good and does not sin.
pass_b_english: Under the gracious covenant Baron names some regenerate sins ‘venial’: they do not cut kingdom-hope or prior favor-degree.
He classes involuntary lust-motions, work-adhering blemishes, and small-matter faults—backed by James, John, and Ecclesiastes on universal stumbling.
